title: The Great Gatsby
author: F. Scott Fitzgerald
description: Set in the Jazz Age on Long Island, the novel depicts narrator Nick Carraway's interactions with mysterious millionaire Jay Gatsby and Gatsby's obsession to reunite with his former lover, Daisy Buchanan. A timeless portrait of the American Dream, wealth, class, and the hollowness of the elite.

title: To Kill a Mockingbird
author: Harper Lee
description: Told through the eyes of young Scout Finch, this Pulitzer Prize-winning novel explores racial injustice and moral growth in the Deep South during the 1930s. Lawyer Atticus Finch defends a Black man wrongly accused of a serious crime in a landmark act of courage and integrity.

author: George Orwell
description: In a totalitarian superstate, Winston Smith works for the Ministry of Truth rewriting history. His secret rebellion against Big Brother and the oppressive Party leads him into a love affair and ultimately a terrifying confrontation with power. A cornerstone of dystopian literature that remains startlingly relevant.

title: Brave New World
author: Aldous Huxley
description: Set in a futuristic World State of genetically modified citizens and an intelligence-based social hierarchy, Bernard Marx and Lenina Crowne visit a 'Savage Reservation' and bring back a man born naturally who challenges everything their society stands for. A prophetic and unsettling vision of a consumer culture taken to its extreme.

title: Dune
author: Frank Herbert
description: On the desert planet Arrakis, young Paul Atreides must navigate treacherous politics, religion, and survival after his family is betrayed and he is thrust into the role of messianic leader to the native Fremen. The most celebrated science fiction novel of all time and a masterpiece of world-building.

title: The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy
author: Douglas Adams
description: Seconds before Earth is demolished to make way for a hyperspace bypass, Arthur Dent is swept off the planet by his friend Ford Prefect, a researcher for the eponymous interstellar guidebook. What follows is a beautifully absurd comic adventure through space, time, and the ultimate question of life.

title: Neuromancer
author: William Gibson
description: The founding text of cyberpunk fiction. Washed-up computer hacker Henry Case is given one last chance: a mysterious employer needs him to pull off the ultimate hack — a run on the Tessier-Ashpool AI construct. Gibson's debut novel coined the word 'cyberspace' and redefined what science fiction could be.

title: Project Hail Mary
author: Andy Weir
description: Ryland Grace wakes up alone on a spaceship millions of miles from Earth with no memory of how he got there. As his memories slowly return, he realises he is humanity's last hope to save the world from an extinction-level threat. A thrilling, scientifically rigorous adventure full of heart and humour.

title: Sapiens: A Brief History of Humankind
author: Yuval Noah Harari
description: From a renowned historian comes a groundbreaking narrative of humanity's creation and evolution. Harari explores how Homo sapiens came to dominate the planet through cognitive, agricultural, and scientific revolutions, challenging our most fundamental ideas about ourselves, our societies, and our place in the world.

title: Thinking, Fast and Slow
author: Daniel Kahneman
description: Nobel laureate Daniel Kahneman reveals the two systems that drive the way we think: System 1 is fast, intuitive, and emotional; System 2 is slower, more deliberative, and more logical. Kahneman exposes the extraordinary capabilities—and the faults and biases—of fast thinking, and the pervasive influence of intuitive impressions on our thoughts and behaviour.

title: Educated
author: Tara Westover
description: Born to survivalists in the mountains of Idaho, Tara Westover was seventeen the first time she set foot in a classroom. Her quest for knowledge transforms her, taking her from the peaks of the Rockies to Cambridge and Harvard. A remarkable, universal story about the power of education to open possibilities and change lives.

title: Atomic Habits
author: James Clear
description: James Clear, one of the world's leading experts on habit formation, reveals practical strategies that will teach you exactly how to form good habits, break bad ones, and master the tiny behaviours that lead to remarkable results. If you're having trouble changing your habits, the problem isn't you—it's your system.

title: Gone Girl
author: Gillian Flynn
description: On the morning of their fifth wedding anniversary, Amy Dunne disappears. Her husband Nick becomes the prime suspect, but the more the investigation unfolds, the less we can be sure of anything. Told in alternating perspectives with unreliable narrators, this is a compulsive psychological thriller that will keep you guessing.

title: The Girl with the Dragon Tattoo
author: Stieg Larsson
description: Journalist Mikael Blomkvist and the enigmatic hacker Lisbeth Salander team up to investigate a forty-year-old disappearance within a wealthy Swedish family. The investigation draws them into a dark web of murder, financial corruption, and sadism. The first instalment of the Millennium series that captivated the world.

title: The Silent Patient
author: Alex Michaelides
description: Alicia Berenson, a famous painter, shoots her husband in the face five times and then never speaks another word. Criminal psychotherapist Theo Faber is convinced he can unlock the truth behind Alicia's silence, and his obsession with her drives him to make a discovery more shocking than he could have imagined.

title: Big Little Lies
author: Liane Moriarty
description: Three women's seemingly perfect lives unravel at a school trivia night, where someone ends up dead. Told through witness testimonies, this sharp, darkly comedic novel about the lies people tell themselves and each other exposes the sometimes fraught dynamics of parenting, marriage, and community.

title: The Name of the Wind
author: Patrick Rothfuss
description: This is the tale of Kvothe—the most notorious wizard his world has ever seen. Now it is his chance to tell his own story. His fictional autobiography is a masterwork of storytelling: a beautifully crafted tale of a young man with an extraordinary gift for magic, music, and trouble.

title: The Way of Kings
author: Brandon Sanderson
description: The first book in the Stormlight Archive series. In a world assaulted by highstorms and Desolations, Kaladin Stormblessed navigates slavery and treachery while Dalinar Kholin, a highprince, seeks to unite his people against a nameless enemy. An epic, immersive world-building achievement unlike anything else in fantasy.

title: Good Omens
author: Terry Pratchett & Neil Gaiman
description: An angel and a demon who have grown fond of life on Earth team up to prevent the Apocalypse. The Antichrist has been born, the Four Horsepersons of the Apocalypse are assembled, and the hellhound has set off—but something has gone slightly wrong. A magnificently funny and oddly moving novel about the end of everything.

title: The Lies of Locke Lamora
author: Scott Lynch
description: Locke Lamora is a con artist in the city of Camorr—a thief so daring that his Gentleman Bastards band targets only the rich, the powerful, and the supremely well-protected. But when they cross a mysterious criminal known only as the Grey King, their game becomes infinitely more dangerous.

title: Steve Jobs
author: Walter Isaacson
description: Based on more than forty interviews with Jobs conducted over two years—as well as interviews with more than a hundred family members, friends, adversaries, competitors, and colleagues—Walter Isaacson has written a riveting story of the rollercoaster life and intense personality of a creative entrepreneur whose passion for perfection and ferocious drive revolutionised six industries.

title: Becoming
author: Michelle Obama
description: In her memoir, Michelle Obama chronicles the experiences that have shaped her—from her childhood on the South Side of Chicago to her years as an executive balancing the demands of motherhood and work, to her time spent at the most famous address in the world. With unerring honesty and lively wit, she describes her triumphs and her disappointments.

title: The Diary of a Young Girl
author: Anne Frank
description: Anne Frank's account of her family's two years in hiding during the German occupation of the Netherlands is one of the most widely read books in the world. A frank, sometimes funny, sometimes devastating chronicle of adolescence and persecution that remains a testament to the enduring human spirit.

title: Know My Name
author: Chanel Miller
description: Known to the world as Emily Doe when she wrote the victim impact statement that went viral in the Brock Turner case, Chanel Miller reclaims her identity in this powerful memoir about survival, trauma, recovery, and the transformative power of art. A lyrical, courageous act of bearing witness and a call to action.
